instrument_name: RCW 49.46 Minimum Wage Requirements and Labor Standards (minimum wage indexation, tips, overtime, exemptions, paid sick leave)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-06-13
figure_or_rule_carried: 49.46.020(2)(b): L&I recalculates the minimum wage each Sept 30 by CPI-W (12 months to Sept 1, Aug-to-Aug), to the nearest cent, effective next Jan 1; (3) all tips and service charges paid to employee, no tip credit; (5) under-18 minimum by rule. 49.46.130: 1.5x regular rate over 40 h/week; agricultural employees 40 h from 2024-01-01 (6)(c); exemptions (2)(a)-(j); retail commission (3); vehicle sales (4). 49.46.210: paid sick leave accrual 1 h per 40 h worked, use from day 90, paid at greater of minimum wage or normal hourly compensation, carryover cap 40 h, no payout on separation (except construction (1)(l)), reinstatement if rehired within 12 months. 49.46.010(4): exclusions incl. casual labor in private home (b), EAP/outside sales (c), volunteers (d), live-in on-call (j), elected officials (l). Page banner on 49.46.010: CHANGE IN 2026 (SEE 2355-S.SL).

instrument_name: RCW 49.48 Wages - Payment - Collection (final pay, deductions, overpayments of public employees)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-08-08
figure_or_rule_carried: 49.48.010(2): on discharge or voluntary quit, wages due are paid at the end of the established pay period (same rule for both; a CBA may provide otherwise). (3): no withholding or diversion unless required by law, agreed orally or in writing, or for medical care, recorded openly. 49.48.160: wholesale sales-rep commissions within 30 days of principal's receipt, also after termination. 49.48.200: public-employer overpayment recovery max 5% of disposable earnings per period (full outstanding in final period) after notice under 49.48.210.

instrument_name: RCW 49.52 Wages - Deductions - Contributions - Rebates (authorized withholding)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-05-12
figure_or_rule_carried: 49.52.060: withholding lawful only when required or empowered by state/federal law, or expressly authorized in writing in advance by the employee for a lawful purpose for the employee's benefit, or for medical/surgical/hospital care with no employer financial benefit and recorded in the books. 49.52.050: unlawful rebates/withholding is a misdemeanor.

instrument_name: WAC 296-126 Standards of labor for the protection of employees (payment interval, deductions, overpayments, statements, personnel files)
authority: Washington L&I (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-07-30
figure_or_rule_carried: -023: wages paid on an established regular pay day at no longer than monthly intervals; pay day no later than 10 calendar days after end of a sub-monthly pay period; monthly period may hold back last 7 days to next pay day; overtime on the regular pay day of the period earned; direct deposit available on pay day. -025/-028: deductions required by law, medical, court orders/child-support notices may go below minimum wage; written advance authorization for employee-benefit deductions; final-period-only cash shortage/breakage deductions not below minimum wage; no employer profit. -030: overpayment recoupment if infrequent and inadvertent, detected within 90 days, advance written notice. -040: itemized statement each payday: pay basis (hours/days), rate(s), gross wages, all deductions; pay period by month/day/year and payment date; separate from paycheck; electronic if employee can access and copy on payday. -050: records kept at least 3 years; personnel file inspection within 21 days; former-employee discharge statement within 21 days of written request.

instrument_name: WAC 296-128 Minimum wages (records, payment interval, EAP salary thresholds, paid sick leave rules)
authority: Washington L&I (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-03-20
figure_or_rule_carried: -020: records kept at least 3 years. -545: EAP/computer-professional salary threshold as multiple of state minimum wage x 40 h: 2026 2.25x regardless of size; 2027 2.25x (1-50 WA employees) / 2.5x (51+); 2028+ 2.5x. -755(2): not less than monthly, written or electronic notice of sick leave accrued, used since last notice and available; may be on the regular payroll statement. -755(1): notice of entitlement at hire.

instrument_name: L&I Minimum Wage page (2026 and 2027 rates, youth 85%)
authority: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 state minimum wage USD 17.13/h; 2027 USD 17.73/h (from 2027-01-01); 14-15 year olds no less than 85% (2027 USD 15.07); tips and service charges cannot count toward minimum wage (RCW 49.46.020(3)); CPI-W adjustment announced Sept 30, effective Jan 1.

instrument_name: L&I news release 26-17 Washington minimum wage rises to 17.73 an hour in 2027 (2026-09-30)
authority: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
figure_or_rule_carried: 2027 minimum wage USD 17.73 (+3.5% CPI-W Aug-to-Aug) from USD 17.13; youth (14-15) USD 15.07 (from 14.56); exempt salary 2027: 51+ employees 2.5x = USD 1,773.00/week (92,196.00/yr); up to 50 employees 2.25x = USD 1,595.70/week (82,976.40/yr); computer professionals hourly 3.5x = USD 62.06 (2026: 59.96); non-compete threshold Jan-Jun 2027 USD 131,326.59 (employees) / 328,316.49 (contractors); non-compete ban from July 2027; localities above state: Seattle, SeaTac, Tukwila, Renton, Bellingham, Everett, Burien, unincorporated King County. instrument_name: L&I Local Minimum Wage Rates (2026)
authority: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 local minimums: Bellingham 19.13; Burien 21.78 (501+) / 20.78 (16-500) / 19.28 (<=15); Everett 20.77 (>500 WA employees), 15-499: 18.77 Jan-Jun then 19.77 Jul-Dec 2026, <=14 not covered; unincorporated King County 20.82 (>500) / 19.82 (16-499, or <=15 with >=2M revenue) / 18.32 (<=15, <2M); Renton 21.57 (>500), 15-500: 20.57 Jan-Jun then 21.57 Jul-Dec 2026; SeaTac 20.74 (hospitality and transportation); Seattle 21.30; Tukwila 21.65 (15+ worldwide etc.). instrument_name: RCW 6.27 Distraint, garnishment (earnings exemption, processing fees, continuing lien)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-10-09
figure_or_rule_carried: 6.27.150 weekly exempt amount: general = greater of 35x federal minimum hourly wage or 75% of disposable earnings; consumer debt = greater of 35x STATE minimum hourly wage or 80% of disposable earnings; private student loan = greater of 50x highest minimum wage in the state or 85%; spousal maintenance (non-26.18) = 50% exempt. 6.27.095: continuing-lien processing fee max USD 20 first answer + USD 10 second answer, deducted from the remainder after withholding; non-continuing writ USD 20 fee paid by plaintiff.

instrument_name: RCW 39.12 Prevailing wages on public works (certified payroll records)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-05-08
figure_or_rule_carried: 39.12.120(1): payroll records kept 3 years from project acceptance: name, address, SSN, trade/occupation, classification, straight and overtime rates, hourly rate of usual benefits, daily and weekly hours, gross wages, itemized deductions, withholdings, net wages. (2): certified payroll filed at least monthly through the L&I online system (or approved format). Complements US-WA-P5-1-002 (39.12.020).

instrument_name: RCW 50A.10 Paid family and medical leave - premiums
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2025-05-15 (last amended 2023 c 116)
figure_or_rule_carried: Premium on wages up to the Social Security wage base (4); employer may deduct up to 100% of the family-leave premium and up to 45% of the medical-leave premium (3); employers with fewer than 50 WA employees owe no employer share (5)(a); total rate set around Oct 20 each year: 140% of prior FY expenses minus fund balance, divided by prior FY taxable wages, rounded UP to the nearest 0.01%, capped at 1.20% (6); employer size = average employees over last 4 quarters as of Sept 30 (7)(c); local PFML programmes pre-empted (10).

instrument_name: ESD - How we determine tax rates (UI components, new employer rate, wage base history)
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
figure_or_rule_carried: Total rate = experience rate + social cost rate (capped 1.22%) + EAF 0.02%-0.03%; experience + social cannot exceed 6%; 40 rate classes by benefit ratio (4 years); new employers 2026 = 115% of industry average, federal minimum 1%; delinquency add-ons 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0%; taxable wage base 2026 USD 78,200 (2025 72,800; 2024 68,500); 2027 wage base not yet published on 2026-11-02; annual rate notice mailed in December. No employee UI contribution stated.

instrument_name: ESD - How to file your quarterly tax and wage reports
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
figure_or_rule_carried: Two quarterly reports: UI tax and wage report (ESD EAMS) and a combined Paid Leave + WA Cares report. UI report per employee: name, SSN, gross pay, hours worked in quarter (rounded up to whole hours; 40/week if salaried hours not tracked; paid leave hours included), Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) code. Due last day of month after quarter end (Apr 30, Jul 31, Oct 31, Jan 31); next business day if weekend/holiday; file even with no payroll. Online (EAMS via SAW, file import) or ESD paper forms only. Corporate officers without voluntary coverage: Exempt Officer section, count and combined wages only. Domestic service: report once USD 1,000 in a quarter, then the whole year. Unregistered quarter penalty greater of USD 1,000 or 2x unpaid tax.

instrument_name: ESD - Reporting new and rehired employees
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
figure_or_rule_carried: Report all new employees within 20 days of hire, and rehires absent 60+ days, to DSHS (Division of Child Support); RCW 26.23.040.

instrument_name: ESD news release: Paid Family & Medical Leave premium rate increases to 1.2% in 2027 (2026-10-16)
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
figure_or_rule_carried: PFML total premium 2027 = 1.2% (2026 = 1.13%); split 2027: employer 29.3% / employee 70.7% of total premium (2026: employee up to 71.43%, US-WA-PFML-001); 2SHB 2345 (2026 session, response to IRS guidance) changes the family/medical distribution of contributions from 2027 without changing the total employee/employer division; employers under 50 employees (size fixed Sept 30) owe no employer share but must collect the employee share; Q3 and Q4 2026 reports use 2026 rate and split. 1.2% equals the statutory cap of RCW 50A.10.030(6)(b)(ii).

instrument_name: WA Cares Fund - Employers page (premium 0.58%, uncapped, exemptions)
authority: WA Cares Fund (DSHS / ESD)
article_or_section: Collecting premiums; Calculating premiums; Tracking employee exemptions
figure_or_rule_carried: Employee-paid premium 0.58% of gross wages (gross x 0.0058), NOT capped at the Social Security wage base; employer pays no share; reported and paid quarterly on the same report as Paid Leave; suggested paystub label 'WA Cares Fund' or 'WA Cares LTC'; employer must not deduct from employees who present an ESD exemption approval letter; some exemptions conditional, employee must notify changes. Local copy of the page cited by US-WA-LTC-001.

instrument_name: Washington DOR - Income tax page (SB 6346, from 2028)
authority: Washington Department of Revenue
figure_or_rule_carried: Washington does not currently have an individual income tax. From 2028-01-01 a 9.9% tax on individuals and joint filers with AGI over USD 1 million (SB 6346, 2026 Legislature); first returns April 2029. Page states no employer withholding mechanism. Local copy re-verifying US-WA-PIT-001.

instrument_name: RCW 26.23 State support registry (new-hire reporting, income withholding orders, processing fee)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2025-09-16
figure_or_rule_carried: 26.23.040: report hires of persons residing or working in WA (new, or rehired after 60+ consecutive days' separation) to the Washington state support registry within 20 days, by W-4 or equivalent; content: employee name, address, SSN, date of birth, first day of paid services; employer name, address, FEIN; electronic reporters may use two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; penalty USD 25 per employee per month (USD 500 if conspiracy). 26.23.060: DCS income withholding order: deduct immediately, max 50% of disposable earnings per pay period; priority over any wage assignment, garnishment or attachment; remit to the WA state support registry within 7 working days of payday; answer within 20 days; employer processing fee max USD 10 first disbursement and USD 1 per subsequent disbursement; federal HHS IWO form used.

instrument_name: L&I Rates for Workers' Compensation page + 2026 Hourly Rates by Risk Classification Code and Fund (xlsx)
authority: Washington State Department of Labor & Industries
figure_or_rule_carried: Hourly (per worker-hour) rates per risk class: Accident Fund, Medical Aid Fund (SAW + MAF NOC), Supplemental Pension Fund (2026 SPF 0.1912 for all classes), composite rate, and 'Payroll Deduction' (worker share, at experience factor 1.0000). Inspected: payroll deduction = 50% x (SAW + MAF NOC + SPF) in 318 of 320 classes (the 2 exceptions, 6901 and 6906, carry no deduction). Example class 101: AF 1.3208, SAW 0.0196, MAF 0.4956, SPF 0.1912, composite 2.0272, worker deduction 0.3532 per hour. Proposed 2027 rates published on the page (final 2027 rates not yet adopted on 2026-11-02).

instrument_name: 2SHB 2345, Chapter 26, Laws of 2026 - PFML contribution allocation (amends RCW 50A.10.030)
authority: Washington State Legislature, via Wayback snapshot 2026-10-16 of lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov
figure_or_rule_carried: Approved 2026-03-11, effective 2026-06-11 (ESD applies the new allocation from 2027 premiums, US-WAS5-015). New 50A.10.030(3): employer may deduct up to the FULL medical-leave premium, and for family leave up to (family premium + 45% of medical premium) minus medical premium; the total employee share stays family + 45% of medical. Rate cap 1.20% and rounding-up rule unchanged; small-employer assistance now cited as RCW 50A.24.030. Also confirms the prior amendment 2025 c 304 s 3. Operating level: payroll withholding split between the two premium lines on the paystub and on the quarterly Paid Leave report.

instrument_name: SHB 2355, Chapter 15, Laws of 2026 - Domestic workers labor protections (Domestic Workers Bill of Rights)
authority: Washington State Legislature, via Wayback snapshot 2026-07-15 of lawfilesext.leg.wa.gov
figure_or_rule_carried: Enacted, takes effect 2027-07-01 (Sec. 17). Hiring entities of domestic workers (4+ hours/month in private residences: nannies, home care, housekeepers, cooks, gardeners etc., incl. independent contractors) must pay at least the state minimum wage and 1.5x over 40 h/week (Sec. 2); no rebates; deductions only if required by law or authorized in writing in advance, documented in writing; written agreement with rate, schedule, payroll deductions, leave benefits, in a language understood by the worker, plus a disclosure of rights (Sec. 3); two-week written termination notice (four weeks in the case set by Sec. 3(3)), with listed exceptions; enforcement by L&I. Sec. 13 amends RCW 49.46.010 casual-labor exclusion. Operating level: wage-payment and labour-standards rule (not tax).

instrument_name: RCW 50.04.320 Wages - Remuneration (unemployment insurance)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-04-21
figure_or_rule_carried: UI wages for contributions = remuneration paid by one employer in a calendar year up to the RCW 50.24.010 base (successor employer counts predecessor wages); includes tips reported to the employer for federal income tax; remuneration = all compensation incl. commissions, bonuses and the cash value of non-cash compensation; excludes reserve/militia duty pay for periods up to 72 hours; settlements for early termination of a written contract are remuneration.

instrument_name: RCW 50A.05.010 Definitions (PFML: remuneration, wages, employment)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-04-23 (last amended 2025 c 178)
figure_or_rule_carried: PFML remuneration (22) = all compensation for personal services incl. commissions, bonuses and cash value of non-cash compensation; EXCLUDES tips, employer supplemental benefit payments on top of PFML benefits, and armed-forces duty pay up to 72 hours. Premium wages (29)(a) = remuneration paid by the employer, capped at the RCW 50A.10.030 maximum (Social Security wage base). Contrast UI (RCW 50.04.320(3)), which INCLUDES reported tips.

instrument_name: WA Cares Fund - Exemptions page
authority: WA Cares Fund (DSHS / ESD)
article_or_section: Exemption pathways; private LTC exemption discontinuation
figure_or_rule_carried: Exemption pathways: living outside Washington; active-duty service member with off-duty civilian job; spouse/registered domestic partner of active-duty member; veteran with 70%+ service-connected disability. Non-immigrant work visa holders automatically exempt from 2026-01-01 unless they tell the employer in writing they want to keep contributing. Private-LTC-insurance exemptees (applied 2021-2022, permanent) may discontinue the exemption between 2026-01-01 and 2028-06-30.

instrument_name: RCW 19.255.010 Personal information - Notice of security breaches
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-10-25
figure_or_rule_carried: A business owning or licensing personal information of WA residents must notify affected residents of a breach without unreasonable delay and no more than 30 calendar days after discovery; notify the Attorney General within 30 days if more than 500 WA residents are affected; a processor holding data it does not own must notify the owner immediately. Applies to payroll data held by an employer or payroll provider.

instrument_name: ESD - Layoffs and employee notifications
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
figure_or_rule_carried: ESD hosts the WARN layoff and closure database; WARN requires 60 days' notice of a mass layoff; Call Center Jobs Act requires notice to ESD before relocating call centers out of the US. The page does not quote the state mini-WARN statute nor a UI separation-notice duty (not located on this page).

instrument_name: ESD - Unemployment coverage for corporate officers
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
figure_or_rule_carried: Corporate officers of for-profit corporations are exempt from WA UI by default; employer must notify uncovered officers in writing that they are not eligible for benefits; employer pays the full FUTA rate (no state credit) on uncovered officers; voluntary coverage may be elected for all officers earning WA wages, then their wages are reported and taxed on the quarterly report; officers owning 10%+ of stock (or related to such an officer) have restricted benefit eligibility. Uncovered officers go in the Exempt Officer section (count and combined wages only, US-WAS5-013).

instrument_name: RCW 50A.35 Paid family and medical leave - employment protection (version effective 2026-01-01)
authority: Washington State Legislature (Code Reviser), via Wayback snapshot 2026-05-18
figure_or_rule_carried: Job restoration after PFML leave applies when the employer has 25+ employees (2026), 15+ (2027), 8+ (2028 onward) and the employee began employment at least 180 calendar days before the leave (replaces the prior 50 employees / 12 months / 1,250 hours test, in force until 2025-12-31); no loss of benefits accrued before leave; highest-paid 10% within 75 miles may be denied restoration under conditions; employer may require fitness-for-duty certification under a uniform policy.

instrument_name: ESD 2026 unemployment tax rates for employers (filterable table xlsx, updated 2026-01-06; PDF table)
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
article_or_section: Sheet 'Tax rate single grid', rate classes 1-40; PDF https://esd.wa.gov/media/pdf/4819/2026-unemployment-tax-rates-employerspdf
figure_or_rule_carried: 2026 qualified employers: experience rate 0.00% (class 1) to 5.40% (class 40); graduated social cost 0.24% to 0.72%; total UI + EAF from 0.27% (0.00 + 0.24 + EAF 0.03) to 6.02% (5.40 + 0.72 = 6.12 capped at 6.00, + EAF 0.02); delinquent employers carry social cost 0.72 plus 0.5/1.0/1.5/2.0 points, up to 8.15% total; non-delinquent deferred-payment contract rates 0.75%-6.15%. Arithmetic re-derived for classes 1 and 40. PDF text extraction is column-misaligned; use the xlsx.

instrument_name: ESD - Employee records you need to keep (RCW 50.12.070, WAC 192-310-050)
authority: Washington Employment Security Department
figure_or_rule_carried: Keep for every employee (also those not reported): name and SSN (with a copy of the Social Security card), SOC code, dates of employment and daily hours, basis of pay, work location, gross pay and deductions per pay period, reason for separation. Retention at least 4 years from the date wages were paid (vs 3 years under WAC 296-126-050 / 296-128-020 for L&I).
